steps.title: Ihram for Umrah at Miqat
steps.instructions: Before crossing the Miqat boundary, perform ritual cleansing (Ghusl), trim nails, and put on the Ihram garments (two white unstitched sheets for men; modest regular clothing for women). Make the intention (Niyyah) specifically for Umrah of Tamattu. Recite the Talbiyah frequently.
steps.location_context: Miqat boundary (e.g., Qarn al-Manazil or Yalamlam depending on direction of travel)
steps.adab: Maintain internal calm, lower the gaze, and increase remembrance of God through the Talbiyah.
steps.safety_notes: Ensure adequate hydration before entering the arid desert travel corridor. Keep emergency contact cards secure.
steps.image_prompt: An educational diagram showing a traveler putting on Ihram garments at a Miqat station, with clear labels for men's and women's attire.
steps.image_caption: Preparing for Ihram at the Miqat boundary.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram showing the correct way to wear Ihram garments for Umrah.

steps.title: Arrival and Tawaf al-Umrah
steps.instructions: Upon arriving at Masjid al-Haram, perform the arrival Tawaf (circumambulation) of the Kaaba seven times counter-clockwise, starting from the Black Stone corner. Men uncover their right shoulder (Idtiba) and walk briskly (Raml) during the first three circuits only. Follow Tawaf with two short rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim if possible.
steps.adab: Move with dignity, avoid pushing others, and maintain personal purity (Wudu) throughout the circuit.
steps.safety_notes: Crowds can be dense. Elderly users should use designated accessible upper levels or wheelchair assistance lanes if needed. Watch for slippery marble floors.
steps.image_prompt: A top-down architectural illustration of the Kaaba showing the counter-clockwise Tawaf path.
steps.image_caption: Performing Tawaf counter-clockwise around the Kaaba.
steps.image_alt_text: Illustration showing pilgrims walking around the Kaaba in a counter-clockwise direction.

steps.title: Sa'i for Umrah
steps.instructions: Walk seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, starting at Safa and ending at Marwah. Men run briskly between the two green fluorescent marker lights. Pace yourself, especially if elderly or fatigued.
steps.location_context: Masa'a (the enclosed corridor between Safa and Marwah)
steps.adab: Recite remembrance and supplication upon ascending Safa and Marwah facing the Kaaba.
steps.safety_notes: The distance is approximately 3.5 km total. Take rest breaks in air-conditioned walkways and drink Zamzam water available along the route.
steps.image_prompt: A cross-section diagram of the Masa'a corridor showing Safa, Marwah, and the green marker lights.
steps.image_caption: Walking between Safa and Marwah for Sa'i.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram of the corridor connecting Safa and Marwah with marked walking lanes.

steps.title: Consummation of Umrah (Halq or Taqsir)
steps.instructions: Complete your Umrah by shaving your head (Halq) or trimming the hair (Taqsir). Women trim approximately a fingertip's length from the ends of their hair. Once completed, exit the state of Ihram. Normal restrictions are lifted until Hajj begins.
steps.location_context: Outside Masjid al-Haram or designated barber areas in Makkah
steps.adab: Praise God for the safe completion of the Umrah journey.
steps.safety_notes: Use licensed barbers using disposable new blades to prevent blood-borne infections.
steps.image_prompt: An educational icon set showing licensed barbers trimming hair with hygienic, disposable equipment.
steps.image_caption: Completing Umrah with Taqsir or Halq.
steps.image_alt_text: Icon set illustrating hair trimming and shaving options for exiting Ihram.

steps.title: Entering Ihram for Hajj on 8th Dhul-Hijjah (Tarwiyah Day)
steps.instructions: On the morning of 8th Dhul-Hijjah, enter Ihram for Hajj from your accommodation in Makkah. Make the intention specifically for Hajj Tamattu. Prepare to depart for Mina.
steps.location_context: Residential accommodation or hotel in Makkah
steps.adab: Renew your spiritual focus, increase patience, and pack essential lightweight provisions.
steps.safety_notes: Double-check identification badges, wristbands, and emergency contact apps before moving out.
steps.image_prompt: A checklist graphic detailing items needed for the transition to Mina.
steps.image_caption: Preparing for Hajj Ihram on 8th Dhul-Hijjah.
steps.image_alt_text: Checklist graphic showing essentials for travel to Mina.

steps.title: Stay in Mina (8th Dhul-Hijjah)
steps.instructions: Travel to Mina and stay there from the morning of the 8th until after sunrise on the 9th. Perform Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr prayers at their proper times, shortening 4-rak'ah prayers to 2 rak'ahs without combining them (according to the majority school; note that some scholarly opinions permit combining).
steps.adab: Engage in personal reflection, Quran reading, and quiet rest to prepare for Arafat.
steps.safety_notes: Stay hydrated in the tents. Memorize your assigned tent block number to prevent getting lost.
steps.image_prompt: A map diagram of the Mina tent city layout with color-coded sectors.
steps.image_caption: Staying in Mina tents on Tarwiyah Day.
steps.image_alt_text: Map graphic showing structured tent blocks in Mina.

steps.title: Standing at Arafat (9th Dhul-Hijjah)
steps.instructions: After sunrise on 9th Dhul-Hijjah, proceed to the plain of Arafat. The standing (Wukuf) at Arafat is the core pillar of Hajj. Combine and shorten Dhuhr and Asr prayers at the time of Dhuhr. Spend the entire afternoon in continuous supplication, repentance, and remembrance until sunset.
steps.location_context: Plain of Arafat and Masjid Namirah / Jabal al-Rahmah area
steps.adab: Face the Qibla where possible, raise hands in humble supplication, and maintain humility.
steps.safety_notes: Heat stroke is a severe risk in Arafat. Use umbrellas, drink oral rehydration solutions frequently, and avoid direct sun exposure during peak afternoon hours.
steps.image_prompt: An aerial schematic of Arafat showing designated tent zones and boundary markers.
steps.image_caption: The gathering at Arafat on 9th Dhul-Hijjah.
steps.image_alt_text: Schematic diagram of the plain of Arafat during Hajj.

steps.title: Departure to Muzdalifah and Night Stay
steps.instructions: After sunset on 9th Dhul-Hijjah, depart from Arafat to Muzdalifah in a calm manner. Upon arrival, combine and perform Maghrib and Isha prayers together. Spend the night under the open sky and collect small pebbles for the stoning ritual (Jamarat).
steps.adab: Rest quietly at night; prolonged individual worship is encouraged, but sleep is also necessary for physical endurance.
steps.safety_notes: Muzdalifah can be crowded and dark. Stick close to your group leader, keep mobile devices charged, and watch your footing.
steps.image_prompt: An illustrative icon showing pilgrims resting under the night sky in Muzdalifah.
steps.image_caption: Overnight stay and pebble collection in Muzdalifah.
steps.image_alt_text: Illustration representing pilgrims resting in Muzdalifah at night.

steps.title: Stoning Jamrat al-Aqaba and Sacrifice (10th Dhul-Hijjah)
steps.instructions: After Fajr in Muzdalifah, move to Mina. On 10th Dhul-Hijjah (Eid al-Adha), proceed to Jamrat al-Aqaba (the largest pillar) and throw 7 pebbles consecutively, saying 'Bismillah, Allahu Akbar' with each throw. Afterward, arrange the sacrificial slaughter (Hadi) through official channels, then shave or trim your hair (Halq or Taqsir) and change out of Ihram into regular clothes (first release).
steps.location_context: Jamarat Bridge facility and Mina slaughterhouses
steps.adab: Maintain orderly movement; avoid aggressive throwing or pushing near the pillars.
steps.safety_notes: Follow designated pedestrian traffic flow directions on the Jamarat bridge to prevent bottlenecks. Vulnerable individuals may delegate the stoning to a trusted representative.
steps.image_prompt: A multi-level diagram of the Jamarat Bridge showing entry and exit pedestrian routes.
steps.image_caption: Stoning Jamrat al-Aqaba on Eid al-Adha.
steps.image_alt_text: Multi-level architectural diagram of the Jamarat Bridge.

steps.title: Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i
steps.instructions: Travel to Makkah to perform Tawaf al-Ifadah (the obligatory Tawaf of Hajj) and Sa'i for Hajj (since this is Tamattu, Sa'i is required again). Return to Mina to spend the nights of Tashreeq.
steps.adab: Perform these rites with gratitude for reaching this stage of the pilgrimage.
steps.safety_notes: Coordinate with group transport schedules as roads to Makkah may experience heavy congestion.
steps.image_prompt: A schematic flow chart showing the transition from Mina stoning back to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah.
steps.image_caption: Returning to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah.
steps.image_alt_text: Flow chart illustrating travel between Mina and Masjid al-Haram.

steps.title: Stoning the Three Jamarat During Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and optionally 13th Dhul-Hijjah)
steps.instructions: Stay in Mina during the days of Tashreeq. Each afternoon (after Dhuhr), stone all three pillars (Jamrat al-Sughra, Jamrat al-Wusta, and Jamrat al-Aqaba) with 7 pebbles each, in sequential order. You may leave Mina on the 12th after stoning (Nafar Awwal) before sunset, or stay through the 13th (Nafar Thani) for extra merit.
steps.adab: Exercise patience in crowded pathways; do not harm fellow pilgrims.
steps.safety_notes: Avoid peak afternoon heat by scheduling stoning during cooler evening or morning hours if permitted by local camp management.
steps.image_prompt: A sequential diagram showing the order of stoning the three pillars: Small, Medium, and Large.
steps.image_caption: Stoning the three Jamarat during the Days of Tashreeq.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram showing the correct sequence for stoning the three pillars in Mina.

steps.title: Farewell Tawaf (Tawaf al-Wada')
steps.instructions: Before departing Makkah to return home or travel elsewhere, perform the Farewell Tawaf (Tawaf al-Wada') as the final act of your pilgrimage. Women who are menstruating or experiencing postpartum bleeding are exempt from this requirement.
steps.adab: Leave the Holy Mosque with a heavy heart, offering silent prayers for acceptance and a future return.
steps.safety_notes: Plan departure times well in advance to accommodate post-Hajj airport or transport terminal queues.
steps.image_prompt: An icon illustrating a pilgrim departing from Masjid al-Haram with luggage.
steps.image_caption: Performing the Farewell Tawaf before departure.
steps.image_alt_text: Icon showing the final farewell circuit around the Kaaba.
